# Gods and Lamb

A chill incremental god-game. Autonomous followers generate Faith; the player
spends it dragging Miracle cards onto them; the village drifts toward Utopia or
Savage Cult. Web and mobile. Cute rounded-cube art, vibrant colour, low
animation overhead.

**`blender/` builds the geometry. `godot/` runs it.** Everything is generated by
Python from primitives, booleans and flat colours — no textures, no hand
modelling, no external assets.

Working here as an agent? Read `AGENTS.md` first.

## The commands

Run from `blender/`:

```
blender --background --factory-startup --python build.py -- look Terrain/grass
blender --background --factory-startup --python build.py -- measure Terrain/grass
blender --background --factory-startup --python build.py -- asset Terrain/grass
blender --background --factory-startup --python build.py -- assets
blender --background --factory-startup --python build.py -- library
blender --background --factory-startup --python build.py -- guards
blender --background --factory-startup --python build.py -- vocab
```

Run from `godot/`:

```
godot --headless --path . --import
godot --headless --path . --script res://tools/village_test.gd
godot --position 2400,1300 --audio-driver Dummy --path . --script res://tools/shots.gd
```

**Always pass `--position 2400,1300 --audio-driver Dummy` to a shot or
probe run.** The tool is deliberately not `--headless` (`get_root().get_texture()` needs a real
swapchain), and `ShotWindow.park()` moves the window off-screen and clears its
focus flag -- but only once the script is running, so without `--position` the
window is still created on top of whatever the user is doing and takes focus
for a moment. The flag pushes it off the corner from the first frame.

**The origin must stay INSIDE the virtual desktop.** `-6000,-6000` is entirely
outside a single 2560x1440 monitor, and Windows then refuses the window:
Godot dies immediately after the "OpenGL API" line, with nothing on stderr and
a meaningless exit code, which looks exactly like a crashing game and is not.
`2400,1300` keeps the origin on the desktop with the body hanging off the
bottom-right. Check `[System.Windows.Forms.Screen]::AllScreens` if the monitor
layout changes. Another session's Godot running in the same project kills
windowed launches the same silent way -- they share `user://`.
`--audio-driver Dummy` mutes it: a probe sweep is fifteen launches, and
fifteen title stings out of a window you cannot see is worse than useless.

Toolchain on this machine:

- Blender 5.2 — `C:\Program Files\Blender Foundation\Blender 5.2\blender.exe`
- Godot 4.7 — `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WinGet\Packages\GodotEngine.GodotEngine_Microsoft.Winget.Source_8wekyb3d8bbwe\Godot_v4.7-stable_win64.exe`

`BUILD.bat` hardcodes both near the top. Edit those two lines for another
machine.

## Non-negotiable rules

**1. Bevel comes after booleans.** Builders make sharp geometry, run every
boolean, then call `soften_all(P)` as the final line. Bevelling first tears the
cut edges.

**2. Weighted Normal must be last in the modifier stack, and cannot coexist
with Smooth by Angle.** `shade_auto_smooth()` adds a nodes modifier Blender pins
to the end; `modifiers.move()` reports success while silently doing nothing. A
WN that is not last does nothing at all. Remove Smooth by Angle, shade fully
smooth, then add WN.

**3. Weighted Normal without a bevel melts the mesh.** Mark edges sharper than
60 degrees as sharp and set `keep_sharp=True`, on the final merged geometry.

**4. Booleans: `solver="EXACT"`, always.** Join cutters first — a six-hole
pattern is one boolean, not six. Apply immediately and delete the cutter.

**5. Build at the origin, standing on z=0, fronting -Y.** Builders never know
where they will end up. The village places them.

**6. Count triangles on the evaluated mesh.** An unapplied Bevel is invisible to
`calc_loop_triangles()` — measured 4.9x understated in the parent project. Use
`kit.evaluated_tris()`.

**7. `export_extras` defaults to `False`.** Without it the GLB is valid,
plausibly sized, and contains none of the `lamb_*` metadata, with no warning.
`verify_export.assert_glb_readback()` exists to catch exactly that.

**8. Never key on Godot node names.** `validate_node_name()` rewrites `.` `:`
`@` `/` `%` to `_`. Key on `get_meta("extras")`.

**9. A brand-new `.glb` must be imported twice.** Godot writes the `.import`
sidecar on the first pass and only then can attach the post-import script.
`build.py` post-patches the sidecar so this is handled, not remembered.

**10. Anything that can fail silently and still save gets an assert.** A render
that succeeds and is empty looks identical to one that worked.

**11. `view_transform = "Standard"`, never AgX.** AgX desaturates and is wrong
for flat stylised work. See gotcha #5.

**12. A cap gets fixed by fixing the geometry, never by raising the number.**

## Before writing any bpy code

Read `blender/docs/02-blender-gotchas.md`. It is inherited from
`C:\Goliath\Robotin` and documents 56 traps in scripted Blender, each of which
produced a visibly wrong result first. The rules above are the subset you will
hit almost immediately.
